title: Precision tapering and eviction-hint protocol for per-token kernel routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: runtime dequant/cast hotspots dominate tail latency for mixed-precision workloads (INT8/FP8). Existing approaches pick a static kernel path per-model or per-batch which leaves per-token work and attention changes unaccounted for. This ticket proposes a precision tapering mechanism: dynamically reduce precision on low-salience tokens and ramp precision back up when attention entropy or routing signals indicate importance. We pair this with an eviction-hint protocol for the KV cache and a lightweight prefetch vault that informs kernel selection without heavy synchronization.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a token-metadata stream with a 200us p99 overhead that contains an importance score and eviction hint.
Kernel selector consumes token metadata and chooses INT8/FP8/FP16 microkernels with <3% additional tail latency vs baseline selection path.
End-to-end p95 latency for small-chat workload improves by >=8% and p99 improves by >=5% on T4-like hardware when precision tapering is enabled.
Dequant op count per decode reduces by >=20% for mixed workloads measured on perf dashboard.
Feature gated behind runtime flag and covered by unit + integration tests and a canary rollout plan.
design_notes: Use a cheap attention-entropy estimator (sliding-window approximate) as the primary token importance signal to decide tapering thresholds.
Eviction-hint protocol: tag KV slots with soft 'keep' scores that degrade over time; kernel selector uses hints to avoid unnecessary repopulation and dequant ops.
Microkernel packing: co-locate tapered tokens into microbatches targeted to INT8 paths to amortize dequant overhead; non-tapered tokens route to FP8/FP16 kernels.
Fallback policy: if token importance spikes mid-decode, trigger a fast re-route that prefers zero-copy kernel handoffs when possible to avoid double-copy dequant costs.
Compatibility: runtime must support models that are precision-agnostic; provide per-model opt-in config and a default conservative policy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement attention-entropy estimator and expose token metadata API (Aisha).
Phase 2: add eviction-hint metadata in KV cache and extend kernel selector to read hints; implement basic tapering policy (Miguel).
Phase 3: microkernel packing changes in serving loop, add fast handoff path for precision upgrades, and telemetry hooks (pair: Miguel + Priya).
Phase 4: perf runbooks, canary rollout, and integration tests against chat/summarization eval suites.
Create feature flag runtime.precision_tapering and console toggle for canary customers.
telemetry: New perf counters: tapered_tokens_count, taper_up_events, taper_down_events, dequant_ops_saved
Dashboard: runtime-precision-tapering/perf with breakdown by model, region, and kernel type
Alert: taper_up_rate spike > 5x baseline for 5m => investigate oscillation/regression
risks: Quality regression: tapering could degrade output quality when importance estimator misfires; mitigate with conservative thresholds and prompt-based evals.
Complexity: additional codepaths increase maintenance surface; keep policy simple and well-commented.
Hardware variance: benefits may vary across GPU types (A100 vs T4); add per-hardware default profiles.
Interaction with caching: eviction hints must not violate correctness for KV reuse; ensure strong invariants in cache access layer.
